solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Keep one's place — international race in view

indicators.note: in says the next pieces are placed inside the word for view

parts.note: a view is a sight
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: An athlete keeps their position as a global race comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Tourist Trophy, a famous motorcycle race held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to stay put and not move from where one is, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Missile to track boat

parts.note: a SAM is a surface-to-air missile
to pan is to track a moving subject with a camera

explanation.surface: A weapon is used to follow and target a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Pan, the film term, means swinging a camera to follow a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flat-bottomed skiff used in China and South-East Asia.

clue.text: Unpunctuality of sailors holding banquets

indicators.note: holding says the word for sailors has the next piece inside it

parts.note: tars is a common word for sailors
dines here is a verb, feasts or banquets

explanation.surface: Seamen are late because they are busy hosting feasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banquets' reads as a plural noun but is the verb, DINES.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lateness, failure to arrive on time.

clue.text: Imprisoned owing to sentence made at the last minute

parts.note: in the nick is slang for in prison
of can mean owing to, as in 'died of hunger'
time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

explanation.surface: A convict's prison term was decided at the very last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the nick' is British slang for prison or a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: just before it would have been too late.

clue.text: Veteran in the lobby produces bag

indicators.note: in places the word for veteran inside the word for lobby

parts.note: a hall is an entrance lobby
veteran as an adjective means old

explanation.surface: An old soldier waiting in a foyer pulls out a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large travelling bag big enough to carry everything.

clue.text: Burn most of the grain found in school

indicators.note: found in says the shortened grain sits inside the abbreviation for school
most of drops the final letter of the word for grain

parts.note: corn is grain

explanation.surface: Most of a school's grain store has been burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the grain's last letter before it goes inside the school abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to scorch is to burn the surface of something.

clue.text: Cover trials only perhaps in a questionable way

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the three words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A newspaper might cover only the trials, a debatable editorial choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges COVER TRIALS ONLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in a manner open to dispute or causing argument.

clue.text: Railway goes over river in the country

indicators.note: in a down answer, going over means sitting above, so the railway piece comes first

parts.note: the Ural is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A railway line crosses a river out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: belonging to the countryside rather than the town.

clue.text: Lots of old invaders keeping Danish leader angry

indicators.note: keeping says the invaders hold the next pieces inside

parts.note: the Huns invaded Europe in late antiquity

indicators.note: the leader of Danish is its first letter

parts.note: red can mean angry, as in seeing red

explanation.surface: Many ancient raiders hold a furious Danish chieftain captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts the leader of Danish and the colour for angry inside the old invaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a very large number, informally speaking.

clue.text: Dog had to be eaten by pig

indicators.note: eaten by says the word had goes inside the word for pig

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A dog had the misfortune to be devoured by a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the animal but is the verb, to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to tail someone secretly, as a detective does.

clue.text: Mark's weary on return! Goodness!

parts.note: M stands for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: on return says the word for weary is read backwards

parts.note: to tire is to become weary

explanation.surface: An exclamation about how tired Mark is when he gets back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodness!' looks like an exclamation but means virtue or worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: worth or excellence deserving praise.

clue.text: See woman smile in opera

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold
hen is slang for a woman
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Look at the lady smiling at the opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Wagner's romantic opera about the swan knight.

clue.text: Accessory upset Celia's orchestra

indicators.note: upset says the letters of the name are knocked out of order

parts.note: the name Celia is the fodder; the possessive 's adds no letter
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A piece of kit upset the orchestra Celia plays in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges CELIA to ALICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hair accessory, a hairband named after Tenniel's Alice.

clue.text: Yardstick for one in command

definitions.meaning: a measuring rod marked in units
a person who governs, such as a monarch

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a straight measuring strip, and a sovereign who governs.

clue.text: Falsify and lie leading to dismissal

indicators.note: to falsify is to alter, so the letters of these two words are altered

explanation.surface: Faking evidence and lying gets an employee sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falsify' rearranges AND LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rejecting a claim out of hand is refusing to accept it.

clue.text: Hesitated with, say, a journalist

parts.note: to aver is to say or assert
ed, short for editor, is a stock journalist

explanation.surface: A journalist dithered, if you like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb, AVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: faltered or was indecisive.

clue.text: Her allies arranged to cause trouble

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of these two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Her friends were organised to stir up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges HER ALLIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to make a noisy disturbance or protest.

clue.text: Notice the French head of state is immaculate

parts.note: to spot is to notice
les is French for the (plural)

indicators.note: the head of state is the first letter of state

explanation.surface: Observe the French president, who looks perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' looks like a president but is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: perfectly clean, without a mark.

clue.text: Writer's offensive relations

definitions.note: read as 'Writer is', with the 's as the link

parts.note: a push is a military offensive
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: An author's relatives are rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective but is the noun, a military PUSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Alexander Pushkin, the Russian poet and novelist.

clue.text: Point dimwit to the French capital

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass
an ass is a fool
au is French for to the

explanation.surface: Direct a fool toward the French capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French capital' suggests Paris, but 'capital' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the chief city of the Bahamas.

clue.text: Vegetable in pot found in rubbish dump

indicators.note: found in says the pot sits inside the dump

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump
an urn is a pot or vase

explanation.surface: A vegetable in a pan has turned up at the dump.
explanation.walkthrough: A TIP is the British word for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a root vegetable with white flesh.

clue.text: Weight carried by horse in match

indicators.note: in places the horse inside the word for match

parts.note: to tone is to match or harmonise, as colours do
a nag is a horse

explanation.surface: A jockey's weight is carried by the horse in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: weight measured in tons, as of a ship's cargo.

clue.text: Look after Athenian leaders first — be there!

indicators.note: first puts the Athenian letters before the word for look after
the leaders of Athenian are its opening letters

parts.note: to tend is to look after

explanation.surface: Care for the city's chiefs before anything else, and be present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Athenian leaders' gives the first two letters, AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be present at an event.

clue.text: Plagiarist is model husband? That is fine!

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
ie, id est, means that is
F stands for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A copycat writer claims to be a perfect spouse, which is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model husband' looks like one phrase but gives T and H separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphor: someone who steals another's work is a kind of robber.

clue.text: Expose oneself to some maudlin curiosity

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone lays themselves open to a little sentimental nosiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: with the clue's 'to', to bring a risk or cost upon oneself.

clue.text: Living without Mike? That's a thought!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the living word goes round Mike

parts.note: sentient means alive and feeling
Mike is M in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Imagine living life without Mike: now there's an idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means outside, so SENTIENT wraps M.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a view or feeling held about something.

clue.text: Food left in hacienda demolished

indicators.note: in places the letter for left among the rearranged letters
demolished says the house's letters are knocked down and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Food was left behind in a ranch house that was torn down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' rearranges HACIENDA; 'in' then puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Mexican dish of a rolled tortilla with a filling.

clue.text: A feudal lord in Belgium

definitions.meaning: a superior to whom a vassal owes allegiance
a city found in eastern Belgium

explanation.surface: A medieval nobleman holding land in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a lord entitled to feudal service, and a Belgian city on the Meuse.

clue.text: Old Bob or Edward put right

parts.note: a bob was a shilling, abbreviated s in old British money
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Either Bob or Edward from years ago fixed things.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a shilling, a pre-1971 British coin written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym, informal: fixed or arranged satisfactorily.

clue.text: Embarrassed about a series of poems being used again

indicators.note: about says the word for embarrassed goes round the poems

parts.note: to go red is to be embarrassed
a cycle is a linked series of poems or songs

explanation.surface: A poet blushes at having reused his verse sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: processed so that material can serve once more.
